slot.brief: Compute the box product [a b c] for given position-type vectors, or use it to find the volume of a parallelepiped/condition for coplanarity; vectors chosen so components are small integers.

stem: The edge vectors issuing from one vertex of a parallelepiped are $\vec a=\hat i+2\hat k$, $\vec b=2\hat i+\hat j$ and $\vec c=2\hat j+\hat k$, in coordinate units. Find its volume.

verdicts.working: Volume = |a·(b×c)|. With a=(1,0,2), b=(2,1,0), c=(0,2,1), b×c=(1,−2,4), so the volume is |1+8|=9 unit³.

working:
$\vec b\times\vec c=\hat i-2\hat j+4\hat k$\n$V=|\vec a\cdot(\vec b\times\vec c)|=|(1,0,2)\cdot(1,-2,4)|=9\ \text{unit}^3$

Independent check: Volume = |a·(b×c)|. With a=(1,0,2), b=(2,1,0), c=(0,2,1), b×c=(1,−2,4), so the volume is |1+8|=9 unit³.
solution:
The volume is the absolute value of the scalar triple product:
$$V=|\vec a\cdot(\vec b\times\vec c)|=|(1,0,2)\cdot(1,-2,4)|=|1+8|=9\ \text{unit}^3.$$
